note: Friday 9 Oct 2026 run, ~07:xx SGT, before Asia's open (SGX 09:00 / HKEX 09:30 SGT). Latest completed US cash session is Thursday 8 Oct close (S&P 500 7,765.36 -0.47%, Nasdaq 27,193.34 -1.25%, VIX 15.41 +2.19% but still low-vol) as crude spiked on intensifying Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz tanker attacks and chip stocks weighed. CNN's own Fear&Greed page again blocked automated fetch (HTTP 451); a confirmed mirror snapshot timestamped Oct 8, 6:42pm ET shows the index dropping sharply to 38 (Fear) from Wednesday's 47 (Neutral) as the hawkish Fed minutes, Hormuz risk-off and a renewed HK-bank-led selloff hit sentiment together. Crypto Fear&Greed eased further to 64 (Greed) from 71 as Bitcoin extended its slide toward ~$81,845. Breadth internals are dated Oct 7-8, the freshest independently confirmed readings: 52-week new lows now swamp new highs (roughly 90-110 highs vs ~400 lows) for the first time this cycle, and the McClellan Summation Index remains deeply negative. Flows have rolled to a fresher weekly BofA/EPFR print (week ending ~Oct 8): the US equity outflow shrank sharply from the prior week's $21.1B to ~$2.7B, while Europe, Japan and EM funds all logged inflows -- a rotation out of the US and into the rest of the world rather than a broad risk-off in fund flows, even as the cash market itself sold off hard on Thursday.
